definitions.explanation: Fruit that has been dried to remove most of its water content, used as a snack, in baking, or as a topping. Includes raisins, dried mango, cranberries, etc.

examples.japanese: ドライフルーツ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦おやつ→おやつ：17921_oyatsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: I eat dried fruit as a snack.

examples.japanese: ⟦ヨーグルト→ヨーグルト：11133_yooguruto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ドライフルーツ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れた→入れる：01098_ireru⟧。
examples.english: I put dried fruit in my yogurt.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦パン→パン：00553_pan⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ドライフルーツ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦ナッツ→ナッツ：11253_nattsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦たっぷり→たっぷり：03404_tappuri⟧⟦{入|はい}っている→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: This bread is packed with dried fruit and nuts.

notes:
A loanword from English "dried fruit" (phonetically adapted as ドライフルーツ). Widely sold in Japanese supermarkets and convenience stores as a healthy snack.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ドライフルーツ{入|い}り: containing dried fruit
- ドライフルーツ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦ナッツ→ナッツ：11253_nattsu⟧: dried fruit and nuts
- ドライフルーツ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{漬|つ}ける→漬ける：09861_tsukeru⟧: to soak dried fruit (e.g., in liquor for baking)
- ⟦{無添加|むてんか}→無添加：19283_mutenka⟧ドライフルーツ: additive-free dried fruit

COMMON VARIETIES IN JAPAN:
- ⟦レーズン→レーズン：12843_reezun⟧: raisins
- ⟦ドライ→ドライ：11147_dorai⟧マンゴー: dried mango
- クランベリー: cranberries
- いちじく: dried figs
- ⟦{干|ほ}し→干す：00115_hosu⟧⟦あんず→あんず：27910_anzu⟧: dried apricots

- ⟦{乾燥果実|かんそうかじつ}→乾燥果実：23987_kansoukajitsu⟧: dried fruit — the formal Japanese equivalent, less commonly used
